items.title: Positive definiteness of the true probability mean

items.statement: Tropp gives matrix-exponential positivity, expectation-order background, and the matrix-MGF existence caution, but does not print this generic standalone lemma or the literal four-family bridge. The author-derived canonical statement is: on any probability space, an integrable finite real matrix field which is positive definite almost everywhere has a positive-definite true Bochner mean; empty finite indices are allowed. Its private literal Gaussian consumer establishes all-real matrix-exponential Bochner integrability, positive definiteness of the true full-law mean, trace/integral commutation, and a strictly positive ordinary trace bounded by r²exp(|s|dR*). This is domain infrastructure, not a matrix-log identity or the source Bernstein conclusion.

formulae.label: Canonical positive-definite true mean
formulae.tex: f\in L^1(\mu;\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)),\quad f(\omega)\succ0\ \mu\text{-a.e.}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\int f\,d\mu\succ0.

assumptions: Let \(\mathcal I\) be any finite index type, including the empty type, and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space. Let \(f:\Omega\to\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)\) be Bochner integrable and positive definite \(\mu\)-almost everywhere. These are the generic P data.

Positive definite means Hermitian with strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector. The mean is the actual matrix-valued Bochner integral under the displayed law. No common positive spectral lower bound is assumed. Empty index types cause no nonzero-vector obligation; P does not add Nonempty.

obligations.label: Author-derived canonical real probability mean is positive definite under integrable AE-PD data, with actual matrix-MGF consumer and omission boundary explicit.

bindings.boundary: The shared probability-mean lemma is author-derived background. Its Gaussian application proves matrix-exponential integrability, positive definiteness of the true mean and the ordinary-trace bound for every real parameter. Matrix-logarithm identities, independence-based MGF estimates, Bernstein concentration, Fact C.6 and the sampling lower bounds remain open.
